definition: Controlling request and token throughput per user and per upstream provider: protecting your capacity, staying within API provider limits, and containing runaway agent loops.
details: Controlling request and token throughput per user and per upstream provider: protecting your capacity, staying within API provider limits, and containing runaway agent loops. Every production LLM outage postmortem eventually mentions this layer.

explainer.lead: Controlling request and token throughput per user and per upstream provider to protect capacity, stay within API provider limits, and contain runaway agent loops. It matters because it is the layer every production LLM outage postmortem eventually mentions.

tiers.eli5: It is like a bouncer limiting how many people enter a club per minute so it never gets overcrowded.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply limits per user and per upstream provider and cap token throughput; a pitfall is omitting bounds on agent loops, letting a runaway process exhaust quota and capacity.
tiers.paperLevel: Enforcement of request and token throughput ceilings per user and per upstream provider, serving to protect capacity, respect API provider limits, and bound runaway agent loops.

explainer.example: Cap each user at 60 requests per minute and cap total tokens per minute to stay inside the provider's quota.
